Large language models (LLMs) have revolutionized AI, but are constrained by limited context windows, hindering their utility in tasks like extended conversations and document analysis. In this paper, we study how to provide the illusion of an infinite context while continuing to use fixed-context models. Our approach borrows from the idea of virtual memory paging that was developed to enable applications to work on datasets that far exceed the available memory by paging data between main memory and disk. This allows for an agent to choose to iteratively modify what is in its context for a single task, thereby more effectively utilizing its limited context.

We propose MEMWALKER, an interactive reading agent which uses iterative LLM prompting to decide which part of the content should be read closely based on its own reasoning. Our approach first builds a structured memory given long context sequence data, and then makes navigation decisions of the pertinent parts to read given a query. This work introduces an efficient method to address this limitation, presenting a novel attention mechanism named Infini-attention. By integrating a compressive memory into the standard transformer architecture, Infini-attention enables the processing of infinitely long inputs with a bounded memory footprint and computational cost. The approach demonstrates superior performance on benchmarks for long-context language modeling, showcasing the potential for broader application in tasks requiring extensive context understanding.
